subject: Post-call: observability evaluation & proposed test stitch-plan
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Rossi <marco@cloudwave.ai>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@atlas.consulting>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: observability evaluation & proposed test stitch-plan

Hi Marco / Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we all have the same plan and priorities. Short bullets first, then proposed next steps.

What we heard from your side:
- Primary goal: get parity with existing hyperscaler telemetry for SRE and product teams (traces, per-request token breakdowns, cost attribution).
- Must-haves: token-level latency, per-route cost, 90/99 latency histograms, retention for 90 days for compliance team.
- Nice-to-have: automatic drift alerts tied to prompt sets and a single dashboard linking model variant -> infra events.

Where Redwood can help (high level):
- Per-request token and cost breakdown (token attribution + tiered retention options).
- Integrated tracing hooks compatible with OpenTelemetry + our KV-cache span tagging for LLM attention flows.
- Dashboards that surface model rollout impacts on tail latency and token cost.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Exact sample rate and retention requirement for traces (you mentioned 1:10 sampling as a starting point).
2) Which hyperscaler telemetry artifacts you want us to correlate (CloudWatch/Stackdriver traces or aggregated perf metrics).
3) A set of 30 representative prompts and target SLAs to run the benchmarks against.

Proposed next steps (short):
- We attach an observability comparison matrix (obs-comparison-matrix.xlsx) that maps feature parity vs CloudWave and a small sample JSON for latency logging. Please review.
- Marissa will propose a minimal test harness (OpenTelemetry + small prod-like workload) and we can run an initial 72-hour run.
- If you can provide temporary read-only CloudWave telemetry keys and a 30-prompt set, we can correlate traces end-to-end.

Would you be available for a short alignment call next Tuesday (30 minutes) to lock the test plan?

Attachments: obs-comparison-matrix.xlsx, redwood-vs-cloudwave-latency-sample.json

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
(a) +1 415 555 0192
From: Marco Rossi <marco@cloudwave.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@atlas.consulting>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: observability evaluation & proposed test stitch-plan

Thanks Aisha — that summary is spot on. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Retention: compliance wants 90 days, but product analytics team wants 1 year for aggregated metrics. Can you confirm options for tiered retention and query performance tradeoffs?
- Sampling: 1:10 sounds reasonable; we may want to do 1:1 for a 24-hour window during the first run to capture tail behavior.
- Hyperscaler artifacts: we'll provide CloudWave traces (OTel format) + aggregated metrics exports (Prometheus). We need to understand how you map those to per-token billing.

I'll pull together a 30-prompt set (mix of short/long contexts + multi-turn) and share them by Monday. Also looping in Elena from Atlas — they're advising on observability and will help evaluate the dashboards.

Can Marissa propose a concrete test harness and timeline? After that we'll approve temporary read-only telemetry keys.

—Marco
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
CloudWave.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Rossi <marco@cloudwave.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: observability evaluation & proposed test stitch-plan

Hi all —

I've sketched a minimal, reproducible harness in the attached matrix and want to call out the technical approach so expectations are clear:

1) Ingestion: we will accept OTel spans from your CloudWave test project and normalize them to our span model (we add LLM-specific spans for KV-cache hits, attention fanout, and compile-time kernel hops).
2) Token-level instrumentation: we will emit a correlated per-token event (lightweight JSON) that references the span_id. This gives you per-request per-token waterfalls in the dashboard.
3) Dashboards: two prebuilt dashboards — (a) Latency & token histogram (p50/p90/p99 by model variant), (b) Cost waterfall + top cost drivers per endpoint. Both can be exported to CSV for your analytics team.
4) Sampling plan: default 1:10 sampling (all spans get the per-token event when sampled). For the first 24 hours of the run we will do 1:1 sampling for the test workload.

Proposed 72-hour test plan (high level):
- Day 0: Deploy Redwood test agent + OTel exporter in your test project; run smoke tests.
- Day 1-3: Execute the 30-prompt set at defined QPS (we recommend 2–5 QPS for representative tail behavior) and collect traces + token events.
- Day 4: Deliver correlation report + redwood vs cloudwave comparison heatmaps.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- p99 tail for production-like prompts <= 700ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) OR clear performance tradeoffs explained and accepted.
- Per-route cost attribution present and reconciles within 5% of your internal billing for the same window.

I attached the obs-comparison-matrix.xlsx and a sample payload redwood-vs-cloudwave-latency-sample.json. Ben — can you add a cost/latency tradeoff column to the sheet?

If that looks good we'll lock schedule and Kevin from infra can provision read-only keys for the test project.

Marissa
Principal Product Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: observability evaluation & proposed test stitch-plan

Hi team —

I've converted Marissa's high-level plan into a step-by-step test checklist and included measurable thresholds so we can qualify this in the sales cycle (tie back to RW-7891). Summary below:

Test checklist (action owner) — target metrics:
- Provision Redwood test sandbox + OTel exporter (Infra / Kevin) — ready in 48 hours.
- Run smoke harness (Marissa) — no failing spans, token events emitted for sampled requests.
- Execute 30-prompt suite at 3 QPS for 72 hours (CloudWave + Redwood harness) — capture spans and per-token events.
- Produce correlation report (Redwood) — includes p50/p90/p99 by prompt bucket, cost attribution reconciliation, and a covariance table showing kernel-choice impact on tail latency.

Acceptance thresholds for qualification:
- Correlation: per-route cost attribution variance <= 5% vs CloudWave billing for the same window.
- Latency: p99 for short prompts <= 700ms OR documented tradeoff + recommended mitigations (batching, quantization, route policy).
- Observability coverage: at least 85% of requests have a trace -> token event mapping in the sampled window.

Logistics asks from CloudWave:
- Read-only telemetry export keys for the test project (limited to 72 hours).
- S3/Blob location for sample request logs (if available).
- Representative prompt set (Marco said he'll share).

If all good, I recommend we schedule the 30-minute alignment call Tuesday and have Kevin provision the keys immediately after. This gives us a clear qualifying artifact to present to your SRE and procurement teams.

Rishi Malhotra
Product Lead, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference
